To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the horizontal merger is a strategic move that can be modeled as an integration of two supply chain networks and that the strategic advantage is the difference between the total cost of the integrated system and the sum of the costs of the two systems.

(i) the strategic advantages associated with a merger are the result of the optimization of the system of firms and (ii) the strategic advantages are a function of the capacity of the firms, the cost parameters of the firms, and the demand parameters of the market.

horizontal mergers between two firms with similar supply chain networks can lead to strategic advantages in terms of reduced total cost, but the gains are not always positive and are not necessarily proportional to the number of firms involved in the merger.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what are the gains from horizontal merger of two supply chain networks?
the quantification of gains associated with mergers and the conditions under which these gains can be achieved.
the quantification of gains associated with the integration of supply chains through the horizontal merger of firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of horizontal mergers, the gains are associated with the integration of the distribution networks of the firms involved in the merger.

the merger is beneficial if it is a merger of two or more firms in the same market with the same technology and if it is a partial merger, in the sense that the merger does not include the entire network of each of the firms.
, in the context of a system optimization, the strategic advantages of mergers are determined by the nature of the supply chain network and the degree to which the merger can exploit it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
horizontal mergers can be a powerful tool for improving the efficiency of the supply chain network.
the strategic advantages associated with the horizontal merger are the result of the optimization of the supply chain networks of the merging firms.
the framework provides a new perspective for the quantification and analysis of strategic advantages associated to mergers in supply chain network integration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
horizontal mergers are not necessarily advantageous.
the strategic advantage of a merger can be expressed as a function of a set of parameters that are related to the characteristics of the pre-merger networks.
the strategic advantages are not necessarily associated with economies of scale or scope, and that the advantages are not necessarily proportional to the number of firms involved in the merger.
